contentBlocks.text: This week you've built a question, sources, and honest notes. Today: organize it all into an outline!

An outline groups your research findings into logical sections before you start writing full paragraphs — it's much easier to reorganize a few bullet points than a fully-written paper. A simple research outline has: an introduction stating your research question, 2-3 body sections each covering one main finding, and a conclusion. Build a simple outline for your own Day 1 research question, with at least 2 body sections.
You just organized your research into a real outline! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Understand an outline's structure: introduction, body sections, conclusion
Build a simple outline for the child's own research question with at least 2 body sections
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review this week's question, sources, and paraphrasing work.
2. Introduce the introduction/body/conclusion outline structure.
3. Have the child build their own outline with at least 2 body sections.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: provide the outline structure as a fill-in-the-blank template rather than requiring the child to build it from scratch
Ready for more: ask the child to add a third body section to their outline
This is the week's synthesis moment — organizing everything built this week into one usable planning document
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended organizing activity — check that the outline includes the child's research question in the introduction and at least 2 genuine, distinct body sections.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 7 Writing standard W.7.7, synthesizing this week's research skills into one organized planning document before tomorrow's review.
